title: Ramayana Presales: Canada and US Diaspora Buy 88,772 Tickets Worth $1.7 Million
excerpt: North America is Ramayana: Part One's biggest overseas market, with premiere shows alone selling 29,175 tickets for $647,400 ahead of the November 5 release.
body:
• North America — the United States and Canada together — has bought 88,772 presale tickets for Ramayana: Part One worth $1.7 million, the largest overseas market for the film.
  • Overseas presales overall have crossed $2.2 million from 116,738 tickets, ahead of the film's worldwide release on November 5.
  • Premiere shows in North America alone account for $647,400 from 29,175 tickets, according to Variety India.
  • For Canadian viewers, the film starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi opens November 5, with presales launched internationally on October 15.

Canada's Indian diaspora is buying Ramayana: Part One tickets in numbers that are outpacing the film's home market on a per-market basis. North America, covering the United States and Canada, leads all overseas territories with 88,772 presale tickets worth $1.7 million, Variety India reported, as the Nitesh Tiwari epic heads toward its November 5 worldwide release.

Overseas beats the early India pace

The makers positioned the film as a global tentpole from the start. International presales opened on October 15, five days before advance booking began in India on October 20, according to Variety India. That head start shows in the totals: overseas sales have reached $2.2 million, roughly Rs 21 crore, from 116,738 tickets, Dainik Jagran reported, an increase of about $374,000 in a single update. North America supplied about 77 percent of that overseas total.

Premiere screenings are a large part of the North American story. Premiere shows contributed $647,400 from 29,175 tickets, Variety India said. In India, by comparison, the film had grossed Rs 13.37 crore from 2.48 lakh tickets in the domestic tally Variety reported, with Maharashtra, Delhi and Karnataka the biggest states. Worldwide advance sales have crossed 4 lakh tickets, according to Dainik Jagran.

The other overseas markets

Australia has recorded $184,000 from 10,938 tickets, while the United Kingdom and Ireland stand at $182,400 from 10,193 tickets. Germany has generated 82,300 euros from 4,275 tickets, and the rest of Europe a further 40,300 euros from 2,560 tickets, both outlets reported. The pattern is consistent: diaspora-heavy markets are booking early and at premium formats, rather than waiting for opening-weekend word of mouth.

The film behind the numbers

Ramayana: Part One is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and backed by Prime Focus Studios and Monster Mind Creations. Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi lead the cast in the adaptation of the Sanskrit epic, scheduled for a grand global theatrical release on November 5, coinciding with the Diwali festive weekend. Our earlier coverage tracked the India side of the same surge, where the film sold 1.33 lakh day-one tickets in the national chains PVR Inox and Cinepolis.

What it means for Canadian audiences

For Indian-Canadian families, the presale rush is practical as much as cultural: premiere and opening-day shows in major Canadian cities sell through first, and the North American premiere tally of 29,175 tickets suggests the best seats for November 4 previews and November 5 shows are going early. Trade trackers caution that presales measure committed fans, not final box office — the film's real test is whether bookings keep building in the final days before release and whether walk-in audiences follow. With nine days counted in Variety India's tally, Ramayana is expected to challenge global box-office records for an Indian film, and Canada is one of the markets doing the heavy lifting.
